items.title: Hertfordshire councils reorganisation: four new councils decided, now on hold
items.time: on hold since early September 2026 (reports date the pause 7 or 8 September); still no new date as of 26 October 2026; Hertfordshire County Council has filed a protective judicial review claim
items.plain: On 16 July 2026 the government chose four new unitary councils for Hertfordshire, starting 1 April 2028. Watford, Three Rivers and Hertsmere would form South West Herts. Dacorum and St Albans would form West Herts. In early September ministers paused and reviewed that decision.
items.detail: The shadow elections planned for May 2027 are cancelled and existing councils' elections carry on. County council leader Steve Jarvis welcomed the review. Councillors voted to seek legal advice on a possible judicial review. Watford's elected Mayor has also issued a statement saying the council awaits the review's outcome. There is no update on Hertfordshire's ambition for a mayoral strategic authority. The statutory consultation ran from 5 February to 26 March 2026. On 7 September 2026, the Deputy Prime Minister and Housing Secretary, Angela Rayner, announced a review of local government reorganisation decisions in every area except Surrey; Essex, Southend and Thurrock, Hampshire, the Isle of Wight, Portsmouth and Southampton, Norfolk and Suffolk had their reorganisations withdrawn outright, while Hertfordshire's July 2026 four-council decision was paused and put under review rather than withdrawn. A 9 September 2026 statement from the Hertfordshire programme's Senior Responsible Officer, Angie Ridgwell, and Dacorum Borough Council's own 8 September 2026 news item, both confirmed the May 2027 shadow elections are cancelled for Hertfordshire. On 3 September 2026, Hertfordshire County Council, alongside Lincolnshire and Newcastle-under-Lyme, sent the Secretary of State a pre-action protocol letter demanding disclosure of the evidence behind the four-unitary decision; the letter stated this was not itself a decision to launch a judicial review. Cllr Jarvis reiterated that the four-unitary model is the most expensive, complex and disruptive option, and that a two-unitary proposal was most popular with consultation respondents. By the 16 October 2026 judicial-review limitation deadline, Hertfordshire County Council filed a protective judicial review claim to preserve its legal position while the government's review continues (Local Government Lawyer, 16 October 2026); separate research by the Local Government Chronicle, published 15 October 2026, found Hertfordshire among 10 of the 19 affected two-tier areas taking similar protective legal action, with the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government saying only that it would 'set out next steps in due course'. Rechecked 20 October 2026: over six weeks after the pause, ministers had still not announced the outcome of the review; the Hertfordshire LGR programme's own news page still showed the 9 September 2026 statement from Senior Responsible Officer Angie Ridgwell as its latest post, with no newer announcement. Rechecked again 26 October 2026: still no change; no outcome of the review has been announced.
items.how: No consultation is open on this. Watch council and government news, including the Herts LGR site and Watford Borough Council's news page, for the outcome of the review.

items.title: Croxley Green, Little Green Lane: 600-home planning appeal
items.body: Developer appeal to the Planning Inspectorate (Three Rivers refused the application)
items.time: inquiry closed; no decision date published; still awaiting the Inspector's decision as of 26 October 2026
items.plain: A developer is appealing the refusal of about 600 homes on roughly 40 hectares of Green Belt at Croxley Green. The public inquiry opened on 27 August 2026 and has closed. The Inspector's decision is awaited.
items.detail: The scheme includes a primary school, a local centre, a country park and 50 percent affordable homes. The council withdrew two of its refusal reasons. An August 2026 national planning policy framework replaced the December 2024 one mid-appeal. The legal agreement includes a £1.065m contribution to TfL. References: PINS 6004972; TRDC 24/2073/OUT; appeal 26/0012/REF. A Change.org 'Save our Green Belt' petition stood at 3,221 signatures on both 12 and 13 October 2026, had risen to 3,254 by 15 October 2026, 3,256 on 16 October 2026, 3,271 on 19 October 2026, and 3,295 when checked again on 26 October 2026. A correction: an earlier version of this card referred to a separate 'Save Little Green Lane' petition with around 2,800 signatures as being about this appeal; rechecking on 19 October 2026 found that petition is in fact a different, older (2021) Change.org petition about the unrelated 160-home Killingdown Farm scheme, which also uses Little Green Lane as an access road, so it is no longer listed here as being about this appeal. Council records cited by campaigners report that 708 of 741 council responses were objections. The date shown on this card is a sort position only. As of 19 October 2026, the Planning Inspectorate's own online appeal tracker for reference 6004972 still showed the appeal as 'closed for comment, awaiting decision' (Three Rivers describes the same reference as app. 24/2073/OUT), consistent with Three Rivers' own planning appeals page, which also says the decision will be published when available; no Inspector's decision had been issued. Rechecked 20 October 2026: the appeal tracker still shows 'awaiting decision', with no change. Rechecked again 26 October 2026: still 'awaiting decision'; no Inspector's decision has been issued.
items.how: The inquiry is over. Watch the Three Rivers planning appeals page, or the Planning Inspectorate's own appeal tracker for reference 6004972, for the decision.

items.title: Three Rivers Local Plan: Regulation 19 consultation (seven Green Belt sites)
items.time: closed 25 September 2026; submission deadline 30 November 2026
items.plain: The final draft Local Plan that the council will send to a government inspector. The Minister directed the council to include seven Green Belt sites.
items.detail: Opened 31 July 2026, closed 25 September 2026. Sites: Kings Langley Estate south, Rousebarn Lane, East Green Street (Chorleywood, within the Chilterns National Landscape), land south of Little Oxhey Lane, land east of Oxhey Lane, land east of Watford Road, and Batchworth Golf Course (conditional on its lease). CPRE figures: over 4,200 homes on 212 hectares. The plan meets about 85 percent of need. Examination is expected in 2027. The council's own consultation page confirms it received a ministerial holding direction in February 2026, superseded by an 18 March 2026 intervention letter setting out nine directions, including a requirement to start this Regulation 19 consultation by 31 July 2026 (which it did) and to include six additional sites. The council's own page, updated September 2026, now says: 'The Regulation 19 consultation has now closed. The council is currently preparing documents for submission of the Plan to the Secretary of State for Independent Examination.' As of 19 October 2026 it had still not yet been submitted. There is still no published confirmation that the February 2026 holding direction has been formally lifted in those words; it appears to have been superseded in practice by the March 2026 intervention letter rather than separately withdrawn.
items.how: The consultation has closed. Watch for confirmation that the holding direction has been resolved, and for the submission and examination dates.

items.title: Three Rivers community governance review, stage 2: do you support changes to your parish?
items.time: 16 October 2026 to 15 January 2027 (no exact closing time published)
items.plain: A second round of consultation on parish and community council boundary changes across Three Rivers, including the unparished areas of Maple Cross, West Hyde, Penn and Mill End, and existing parishes such as Croxley Green, Sarratt and Chorleywood.
items.detail: The original review of just Maple Cross, West Hyde, Penn and Mill End (launched November 2025) was discontinued by Full Council on 14 July 2026 after a very low response rate, and replaced by a district-wide review covering those four unparished areas plus every existing parish in Three Rivers. That first, district-wide round of consultation ran 31 July to 18 September 2026. The council's Policy and Resources Committee met on Thursday 8 October 2026 at 7.30pm to consider a report setting out draft, not final, Stage-2 consultation options: moving the Little Green Lane development site from Sarratt Parish Council's ward into Croxley Green Parish Council's ward; a mapped single-member Heronsgate ward within Chorleywood Parish; and four options for Penn & Mill End and Maple Cross & West Hyde (a new combined parish council, merging Penn & Mill End into Batchworth Community Council and Maple Cross & West Hyde into Chorleywood Parish Council, consulting on two separate new parish councils, or no action). Rechecked 20 October 2026: the council's own district-wide-cgr page and its 'Do you support changes to your parish?' news article both now confirm this second-stage public consultation is open, running 16 October 2026 to 15 January 2027, inviting residents, businesses and community organisations to comment on the proposed changes, suggest alternatives or share additional information; the council says no final decisions have been made. The council's news article describes the headline proposal in general terms as a new parish council for Maple Cross, West Hyde, Penn and Mill End, plus possible changes to other parish and ward boundaries, names and governance arrangements, without repeating the Little Green Lane, Heronsgate or four-option detail from the 8 October committee report, so treat that level of detail with some caution until the consultation's own documents are checked directly. The council's original timetable had new boundaries from 1 April 2027 and elections on 6 May 2027, but those dates were set before the local government reorganisation pause, so treat them as uncertain. Separately, Chorleywood's own Heronsgate and Loudwater boundary review (a different, now-concluded process, previously shown on this dashboard) appears to have already reached final recommendations, agreed by Full Council on 10 March 2026 with new boundaries from 1 April 2026, according to Three Rivers' own community governance review page; the companion haveyoursay.threerivers.gov.uk page for that review has not been updated since February 2026 and still describes it as open, so this dashboard no longer lists it as a separate item.
items.how: Comment via the consultation page before 15 January 2027.

In Amersham, a new disabled bay is added at Piggotts End (outside no. 12). Little Chalfont is not named in this notice.
items.how: The changes are already in force. Formal objections on legal grounds go to the High Court within six weeks of the Order being made (by 23 October 2026); general comments can still be left on the Your Voice Bucks page.

Sarratt Parish Council's news page carries an 8 October 2026 item about crowdfunding a fighting fund against over-development in the village, which does not name this application specifically. Note: a separate, unrelated Church Lane, Sarratt appeal for 20 homes (PINS ref 6002930, Clovercourt (Sarratt) Ltd) was allowed by the Planning Inspectorate on 12 October 2026 — a different site and a different applicant from this 54-home application, and not a sign of how 26/0711/OUT itself will be decided.

items.title: Extending Awaab's Law to private rented tenancies and licensed accommodation
items.body: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
items.time: published 9 October 2026; closes 11:59pm on 18 December 2026
items.plain: The government is consulting on extending 'Awaab's Law', strict legal deadlines for landlords to fix dangerous damp, mould and other hazards, from social housing into the private rented sector and into licensed accommodation such as supported housing.
items.detail: Following the Renters' Rights Act 2025, this 64-question consultation covers applying Awaab's Law to private rented tenancies, applying it to accommodation occupied under licence (including supported housing, homelessness temporary accommodation and care-leaver accommodation), and the costs and impacts on landlords and tenants. It runs for just over 10 weeks from publication and is a national consultation, not specific to West Herts or the Chilterns, but would affect private renters and licensed accommodation here as everywhere else.
items.how: Respond online, by email, or by post; respondents can answer only the sections relevant to them.

The Mayor's written response said the former station land is safeguarded for transport use in the Local Plan, that an infrastructure-levy-funded feasibility study has assessed several route options (a guided tram currently scores best on value for money), that no option has been chosen, and that Hertfordshire County Council was said to be preparing a public consultation on route options.
